Per the researcher's limitations, github.com blob URLs for the Element 84 README and the two Microsoft PlanetaryComputerDataCatalog doc source files were fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com instead, since the rendered github.com page needs JavaScript; content matches the cited blob path.

Per the researcher's limitations, Microsoft Planetary Computer's dataset, docs and terms pages, and Google Earth Engine's developer-guide pages, were not independently re-fetched from planetarycomputer.microsoft.com or developers.google.com/earth-engine/guides beyond confirming they are JS-only shells; claims for those two candidates were checked against the STAC API responses and the GitHub-hosted documentation source files instead, matching the researcher's own approach.
The Legal Notice on the use of Copernicus Sentinel Data and Service Information is a PDF; it was fetched with curl and converted to text with pdftotext for quote verification.

The AWS S3 request price and AWS Data Transfer price were verified directly against the AWS Price List offer files for eu-central-1 (SKU-level price dimensions and offer-file version numbers), not against the JavaScript-rendered aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/ page, matching the researcher's own approach.

Page titles were checked against each source's recorded title for substance rather than exact string match; several Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem documentation pages render a generic '<Page> – Documentation' <title> tag and the Google/AWS/GitHub pages append a site-name suffix, but every title matches its source's declared subject with no material mismatch found.
No image asset bytes were read, no requester-pays bucket was contacted, no credentials were used, and no package was installed, consistent with the bounds of this check.

One item per STAC collection was checked against the same single sampled item the researcher recorded (Texas-coast bounding box, accessed 2026-09-09); this check re-fetched each search query fresh rather than trusting the researcher's transcription, and the returned item ids, properties and asset structures match what the research file reports.

Two claim pairs describe genuinely conflicting sources rather than checker uncertainty: the AWS registry (no-sign-request) versus the Sinergise readme (Requester Pays) for the sentinel-s2-l2a bucket, and the Sentinel Hub L2A page's own Basic Facts table (October 2016) versus its Endpoint Locations table (November 2016) for the European coverage start. Both sides of each conflict were independently fetched and read; see the corresponding check records' reasons for which source states which fact.

No claim in this dimension required a corrected or not_verifiable verdict: every cited quote was found verbatim (whitespace and, in one case, HTML-entity decoding aside) on its cited page or in its cited JSON/PDF, and every value, unit and note follows from the quoted text.

Two of the seven newly checked draft claims (both operator claims) rest on a registry page's 'Managed By' section, which names who manages the registry entry, not who owns or operates the underlying S3 bucket; a case-insensitive search of both registry.opendata.aws/sentinel-2-l2a-cogs/ and registry.opendata.aws/sentinel-2/ for the word 'owner' found no match on either page, so bucket ownership stays unstated by these sources for both routes.

The Sinergise readme at roda.sentinel-hub.com/sentinel-s2-l2a/readme.html names no operator for the sentinel-s2-l2a bucket; it gives only a Sentinel Hub forum contact and a Copernicus/AWS Public Datasets license line, so the source_dataset claim's producing organization rests on the registry page's Copernicus OpenHub reference, not on an explicit operator statement.
